name: Gaine

attributes.attribute: was called learned, a seer, and a chief druid
named the hill Uisneach, meaning over somewhat
cut off the tongues of the other druids and buried them on Uisneach

sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Part II. Vol. IX. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd., 1906–1924.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gaine was an Irish heroine in the Dindshenchas, the place-poems of ancient Ireland. One account calls her learned, a seer, and a chief druid. How she composed and prophesied stays unclear, for she never spoke a word. Gaine named the central hill of the land, Uisneach, meaning over somewhat. Her student, the powerful druid Mide, had cut off the tongues of Ireland's other druids. He buried them on the hillside and sat over them.

okr.objective: Record Gaine and her naming of the hill Uisneach.
key_results: Present Gaine as a learned seer and chief druid from the Dindshenchas.
Explain why she could only be named, not quoted, in the account.
Describe Mide's act of cutting off the other druids' tongues.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore, 2008, drawing on Gwynn, The Metrical Dindshenchas.
